name: Istanbul and Rhodes cloudbursts
as_of: 19 Oct 2026 (death toll: Euronews, 19 Oct; rainfall and Rhodes: reports of 15–16 Oct)
headline: Istanbul's heaviest rain since records began in 1942 shut the city down; on the same day Rhodes received 202 mm in about six and a half hours. The weather system behind both has not yet been described in detail by the met services, so this entry stays open.
numbers: Istanbul and Kocaeli combined: at least 8 dead and one missing by 19 Oct (Euronews); Rhodes: 1 dead (earlier report, not rechecked)
timeline: Rhodes: thunderstorms over the north of the island; 202 mm between 06:30 and 12:50 at the NOA station. Four cars swept into the sea at Stegna; one man killed.
Istanbul: rain begins in the morning and intensifies all day. Flash floods in Sarıyer and elsewhere; a 14-year-old electrocuted in Balat; flights diverted; schools closed to Monday.
Rhodes mayor requests a state of emergency; Istanbul deaths rise to three or four.
More heavy rain forecast for Istanbul over the weekend.

sections.The setup: A warm but not record-warm sea: the eastern Mediterranean was 24.3 °C (+0.98 °C) on 1 October (OISST), after a record-hot summer in the central Mediterranean (+2.5 °C). Warm water in October supplies moisture and instability to the first autumn troughs.
sections.The trigger: Slow-moving, electrically intense thunderstorm clusters, typical of a cold upper trough or cut-off low crossing the warm Aegean and Black Sea. The specific synoptic system has not been published yet.
sections.What amplified it: Steep, short catchments on Rhodes; dense urban surfaces, underpasses and basement dwellings in Istanbul; storms that stalled for hours over the same area.
sections.Climate signal: No study. Physical reasoning: a warmer Mediterranean feeds heavier autumn downpours.
sections.Still open: The meteorological cause, final rainfall totals, the weekend rain, and the death toll. This will be completed when Turkish (MGM) and Greek (NOA, EMY) analyses are published.
